MARKET MECHANICS
What is Market Maker?

Published by TradeHQ. Site creator and editorial approach: Anuga Weerasinghe. This page has no recorded editorial review date.

DETAILED DEFINITION

A market maker quotes prices at which it is prepared to buy and sell under applicable venue rules. The ask-minus-bid difference is a quoted spread, not a guaranteed realized profit. Quotes can change; fills, inventory price changes, hedging and operating costs affect results. Obligations and permitted conduct differ between markets. A decentralized automated market maker is a different mechanism that applies a pool pricing rule rather than the same dealer quoting arrangement. Do not infer that a displayed quote will fill an arbitrary quantity or that a market maker always earns money. TradeHQ does not reproduce order queues or dealer inventory.

HOW IT WORKS

A market maker posts bid and ask quotes under venue rules to facilitate trading. A quoted spread is not guaranteed profit, and obligations vary by market.

KEY POINTS
Quote bid and ask prices under venue rules; liquidity is not guaranteed for every order
A quoted spread is not guaranteed net profit
AMMs on decentralized exchanges use algorithms instead of human market makers
💡 WHY THIS MATTERS

Compare quoted bid and ask prices with actual executions. Spread changes can have multiple explanations and do not establish a participant’s intent or sophistication.

Worked exercise and its limits

Hypothetical quotes: buy at $10 and sell at $10.02. Buying 100 units then selling them all at that ask earns $2 gross only if both executions occur. Inventory loss, hedging and costs can exceed that spread; a quote is not guaranteed profit.

References and scope
SEC Investor.gov — market participants and market makers
